blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-verified at Berachain block 24601923 (2026-08-08T19:49:22Z) against the verified multi-collateral DebtToken source. The canonical NECT deployment remained direct bytecode with a zero EIP-1967 implementation slot. Ordinary transfer and transferFrom have no blacklist or pause check, but burn(address _account,uint256 _amount) calls _burn(_account,_amount) without allowance for any caller in denManagers or PSMBonds. The WBERA DenManager 0xf1356cb726c2988c65c5313350c9115d9af0f954 remained actively whitelisted, and a fixed-block eth_call from that address to burn an unrelated address with amount zero succeeded, proving the live authorization path; the constructor PSMBond placeholder 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead also remained whitelisted. The reviewed 4-of-7 Safe behind the three-day owner path can additionally whitelist another PSM bond. NECT therefore has a current direct arbitrary-holder burn capability even though ordinary transfers remain open and the present DenManager uses it for protocol mechanics.

branches.label: WBERA collateral branch
branches.summary: WBERA collateral branch uses the central Beraborrow PriceFeed and a configured RedStone BERA/USD adapter external price source for collateral health and liquidation.

feeds.path: RedStone BERA/USD adapter answer -> Beraborrow PriceFeed -> Collateral Vault/DebtManager ICR

branches.fallbackBehavior: PriceFeed requires valid current and previous oracle rounds, rejects stale answers and over-50% consecutive-round moves, and reverts rather than invoking an alternate live provider.

collateralParameters.note: Active with positive system debt at pinned block 24033076; MCR is enforced by this DenManager branch.

branches.liquidationMechanism: LiquidationManager permits public liquidation below branch MCR. The Liquid Stability Pool first offsets NECT debt against seized collateral; any uncovered debt and collateral are redistributed to active positions in the branch.
branches.backstop: The global Liquid Stability Pool is the first-loss backstop. When deposits do not cover a liquidation, the DenManager redistributes the residual debt and collateral across active positions.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Oracle reads revert when the configured source is stale, invalid, or exceeds the PriceFeed consecutive-round deviation check; the reviewed contracts expose no alternate live feed. A sunsetting branch disables new borrowing and collateral handoff to the Stability Pool while existing positions and redistributed debt remain.
